worlds.name: Hörsaal
worlds.note: The documented system. New surfaces inherit this.

worlds.name: Neumorphic (incumbent)
worlds.note: Not deprecated and not scheduled for migration. Recorded so Hörsaal tokens are never applied to these pages, and neumorphic tokens never to index.html.

board.provenance: Sampled from bpzcalc.jpg (user's own photographed chalkboard); darkest chalk-free patches read rgb(39,41,35), warm olive-grey with red≈green>blue, then deliberately lifted in value so it reads as a board in a lit room rather than a screen in a dark one.

chalk-faint.usage: Non-text only: rules and nav chrome. Barred from text runs.

chalk-blue.usage: Every link. The stick that means 'you can open this'.

chalk-ochre.usage: The 'live' stick: section addresses, active nav state, drawn bullets, disclosure strokes, email keys, focus ring, hover box trace.

rule.usage: Bone chalk at 20% alpha. List dividers, module bottoms, colophon top.

rule-mid.usage: Bone chalk at 34% alpha. Section-head rule, index bottom, ledger leaders, quiet box outline.

rule-strong.usage: Bone chalk at 58% alpha. Drawn box outlines and the skip link.

display.purpose: ALEJANDRO, once, on the photographed board. Expanded chalk caps; the only display-scale text on the page.

headline.purpose: Section titles. Expanded, tracked out and uppercased, because a board title is drawn large rather than weighted heavy.

title.purpose: Project and resource entry names in bone chalk, on the ledger line.

body.purpose: All running prose, capped at a 66ch measure (58ch for the hero bio).

label.purpose: Uppercase micro-labels: ochre email keys, §4 category headings, section tallies, university tags.

chalk-hand.purpose: Caveat, background chalk plane only. Never interface text, never information the visitor must read.

extensions.shadowPolicy: This system has no shadows. No box-shadow and no text-shadow exists in board.css. Depth is material and tonal only: slate layers, vignette, scrims, the deep-slate index recess, and the colophon board foot. Blur appears only as chalk dust (2.5px on the advancing edge) and as a scrim softener (7px behind the display name) — never as elevation.

motion.name: ease-chalk
motion.purpose: The only easing curve in the world. Chalk arrives fast and settles long.

motion.name: write
motion.purpose: Section arrival: heads, titles, tallies, and the writes-across / writes-down leaves.

motion.name: write-fast
motion.purpose: The short end of the writing scale.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Link colour, nav border, box outline and icon-stroke state changes.

motion.name: writes-across
motion.purpose: Single-line arrival, left to right, the way a hand crosses the board.

motion.name: writes-down
motion.purpose: Wrapped-prose arrival, line accumulating under line. A left-to-right wipe across wrapped text uncovers every line's left edge at once and reads like a curtain.

motion.name: stagger-tier
motion.purpose: Per-block stagger inside an arriving section.

motion.name: stagger-leaf
motion.purpose: Per-leaf stagger within a block. Containers carry no ink and arrive without ceremony.

motion.name: reference-write
motion.purpose: References writing in when a disclosure opens — the same hand at the same speed as everything else.

breakpoints.name: lap
breakpoints.note: Masthead collapses to one column; the index becomes a single horizontally scrolling line.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.note: Body 1rem; all multi-column lists to 1; ledger leaders off; section tally to its own row; chalk plane to 1.15rem with wide equations removed.

performance.constraint: Scroll-linked offsets are measured once per layout; the scroll handler performs zero layout reads. A per-frame getBoundingClientRect() across ~50 chalk lines is ~50 forced reflows per frame.

resilience.armedEntrance: The .js class is set synchronously in <head> so the armed state holds from first paint, with a 3s failsafe that removes it if chalkboard.js never boots. Without the failsafe a script failure leaves the page permanently blank.

rasters.role: The masthead board top; the user's own photographed chalkboard and BPZ calculation. Source of the slate colour sample.
rasters.treatment: brightness(1.34) contrast(1.16) saturate(0.66), dissolved into the slate through a single mask.

rasters.role: The pinned print in the masthead: the user at a whiteboard.
rasters.treatment: grayscale(0.72) contrast(1.1) brightness(0.8) under a soft-light board-tinted overlay.

review.round1: six material findings, all scored resolved
review.round2: two regressions plus three contrast failures, all scored resolved; disposition `ship` scoped to those eight fixes
review.mechanicalDetector: returned [] but ran DEGRADED (regex fallback, no computed contrast). Its clean result is an undercount, not a guarantee.

notCanonized: Inline onclick="toggleModule(this)" handlers and the global window.toggleModule they bind to — shipped implementation, not a system rule.
ul.project-list br { display: none; } — a stylesheet patch over authored markup, not a form rule.
extensions.contractGap: The direction contract's OWN-WORLD block states "no radius." The build ships three asymmetric hand-drawn corner values on boxed links and social marks. The build wins; the intent survives as "no rounded container," which the build does honour.

narrative.overview:
The page is not a site about a mathematician; it is his board. One continuous slate runs masthead to colophon, with yesterday's derivation ghosted behind today's argument. There is no card, no panel, no container and no shadow anywhere in this world. Hierarchy is built entirely from four devices: full-measure hairline rules, indentation, scale, and case. When something needs to be set apart, it gets a rule above it and a section address beside it — never a box around it.

The slate #333C36 is sampled from bpzcalc.jpg, Alejandro's own photographed chalkboard, whose darkest chalk-free patches read rgb(39,41,35) — a warm olive-grey where red ≈ green > blue. The shipped value is that measurement deliberately lifted in lightness: a board in a lit room, not a screen in a dark one. That lift is the load-bearing decision of the whole palette. Near-black ground plus a saturated accent is the terminal console, and the console is the confirmed anti-reference. Emissive or glowing text, saturated green, and monospace type are all out of this world by decision.

Depth is material, not elevation. The slate carries a real dust grain, two eraser smudges, arcing wipe-bands, room light falling from the upper left, and the vignette of a surface that curves away at its edges — six fixed, cheap layers, none of them a gradient standing in for a material. Blur exists in this world, but only as chalk dust and as the soft edge of a scrim; it is never a drop shadow and never a glow. The one raster rule is that photographs are graded into the room's light before they are allowed on the board.
keyCharacteristics: One continuous slate: no card, no panel, no container, no box-shadow, no text-shadow, no glass.
Hierarchy from rules, indentation, scale and case only.
Two type families total, no third: Archivo for every word of interface, Caveat for the board's residue.
One motion device for the entire page: clip-path, in two orientations. No opacity fade exists anywhere.
Chalk-tray palette: bone for text, blue for links, ochre for what is live — three sticks, nothing else.
Every radius in the world is an asymmetric hand-drawn corner; there is no rounded container.

rules.name: The Three Sticks Rule
rules.body: The tray holds bone, blue and ochre. Blue means you can open this; ochre means this is live or this is where you are; bone is everything else. A fourth hue never enters the world, and neither accent is ever used decoratively.

rules.name: The No Border Colour Rule
rules.body: Borders and rules are chalk at low alpha, never a colour of their own. If a divider needs drawing, it is --rule, --rule-mid or --rule-strong — a hairline of chalk dust on slate, not a stroke of grey.

rules.name: The Measured-Render Rule
rules.body: Contrast in this world is verified against the shipped render — glyph extents, pseudo-elements intact, worst background patch under each text run — never computed from token pairs. The ground is a photograph under a soft-edged scrim; a token-pair calculation does not describe it. Body text clears 7:1 measured; secondary interface text clears 5:1; --chalk-faint clears neither and is barred from text.

rules.name: The Not-A-Console Rule
rules.body: Never take the ground below the shipped slate toward black, never make chalk emissive (no text-shadow glow, no saturated green), and never set interface text in a monospace face. The lift from rgb(39,41,35) to the shipped slate is the entire difference between a lecture hall and a terminal.

rules.name: The Two Families Rule
rules.body: Archivo and Caveat. There is no third face, and Inter — the incumbent world's face — is deliberately absent from Hörsaal. If a new surface seems to need another family, it needs the width axis instead.

rules.name: The Width-Before-Weight Rule
rules.body: Emphasis at large sizes comes from the wdth axis and from case, not from stacking weight. Above ~1.25rem, expand and capitalise before reaching past 700.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set globally. Counts, tallies and section numbers line up down the page because this is a document of quantities.

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Scrim Rule
rules.body: Every scrim spans the full viewport width using left: calc(50% - 50vw); width: 100vw with vw-based gradient stops, and fades out at both the left and right viewport edges as well as top and bottom via mask. A scrim drawn at shell width with a horizontal fade leaves a visible vertical seam down both sides of every section: a soft-edged panel is still a panel.

rules.name: The Open Board Rule
rules.body: The gaps between sections are open slate at full strength. Scrims belong to text runs, not to the page; scrim the whole column and you bury the board it sits on.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs separation, give it a rule, a scrim, or more space — never a shadow, never a glow, never a translucent glass panel.

rules.name: The Graded Photograph Rule
rules.body: A raster is admitted only after it is graded into the room's light. whiteboard.png runs grayscale(0.72) contrast(1.1) brightness(0.8) under a soft-light board-tinted overlay; bpzcalc.jpg runs brightness(1.34) contrast(1.16) saturate(0.66) and dissolves into the slate through a single mask, not a stack of gradient stops — stacked stops band visibly across a 500px ramp and read as two materials butted together instead of one board. An untreated daylight photograph at full saturation is a foreign object stuck to the slate.

rules.name: The Drawn Corner Rule
rules.body: If something is boxed, its corners are asymmetric and never meet cleanly. A uniform border-radius on a container does not exist in this world at any value.

rules.name: The Hand Not The Glyph Rule
rules.body: Bullets, markers and rules are drawn with pseudo-elements and borders. Brand marks are the platforms' own SVGs; where no platform mark exists, one is drawn to match the set rather than substituted with a stock glyph.

rules.name: The One Motion Device Rule
rules.body: Everything on this page arrives by clip-path, in two orientations: .writes-across for single-line things, .writes-down for wrapped prose. A left-to-right wipe across wrapped text uncovers every line's left edge at once and reads like a curtain rather than a hand — so the orientation is chosen by the shape of the text, not by taste. No opacity fade exists anywhere on this page. Timing is --write 620ms / --write-fast 360ms on --ease-chalk cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1): chalk arrives fast and settles long.

rules.name: The Armed Entrance Rule
rules.body: Any first-paint-hidden state is keyed on a .js class set synchronously in <head>, paired with a 3s failsafe that removes it if the script never boots. Without both halves, a script failure leaves the page permanently blank.

rules.name: The Containers Carry No Ink Rule
rules.body: Only leaves (p, li, h3, .module-item) are armed and staggered; wrappers arrive without ceremony. Stagger is 70ms per tier capped at 8 tiers and 42ms per leaf capped at 16 leaves, after a 150ms lead.

rules.name: The Reduce Don't Erase Rule
rules.body: Under prefers-reduced-motion, travel, scroll-linked writing and staggered choreography go; colour, the chalk plane and the board itself stay. The formulas are simply already written — the way a board looks when you walk into the room after the class.

dos: Do build hierarchy from full-measure hairline rules, indentation, scale and case.
Do draw every rule and border as bone chalk at low alpha (--rule / --rule-mid / --rule-strong).
Do reserve ochre for what is live or currently addressed, and blue for anything that opens.
Do verify contrast against the shipped render with pseudo-elements intact, using the worst background patch under each text run.
Do span scrims the full viewport width with vw-based stops and fade all four edges.
Do grade every photograph into the room's light before it goes on the board.
Do use clip-path for arrival, in whichever of the two orientations the text's shape calls for.
Do open disclosures with grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr and keep the grid item's padding on its child.
Do measure scroll-linked offsets once per layout, so the scroll handler performs zero layout reads.
Do pair any first-paint-hidden state with a boot failsafe that reveals it if the script dies.
Do leave the incumbent light world in style.css and vectorfield.js exactly as it is when editing Hörsaal.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow or a text-shadow — this world has neither, at any elevation.
Don't put a card, panel or glass surface on the board; a soft-edged panel is still a panel.
Don't apply a uniform border-radius to a container. The only radii are the three asymmetric drawn-corner values.
Don't use --chalk-faint for any text run; it is ~3.4:1 on the slate and is reserved for rules and nav chrome.
Don't take the ground toward black, make chalk emissive, introduce a saturated green, or set interface text in a monospace face — that is the terminal console, and the console is the anti-reference.
Don't introduce a third type family, and don't bring Inter (the incumbent world's face) into Hörsaal.
Don't animate anything with an opacity fade; there is not one on the page, and adding one breaks the single motion grammar.
Don't call getBoundingClientRect() inside a scroll or requestAnimationFrame handler.
Don't open a disclosure with a JS-measured max-height.
Don't use a • glyph or an icon font; bullets and markers are drawn strokes and brand marks are real SVG.
Don't apply Hörsaal tokens to thinking-in-measures.html, auctiva.html or tim-posts/*.html, and don't apply style.css's neumorphic tokens to index.html. The two worlds share nothing.
